what_its_for: Risedronate is used to treat and prevent osteoporosis (weak, brittle bones) in women after menopause and in men. It is also used to treat osteoporosis caused by long-term steroid use, and a bone disease called Paget's disease. It works by slowing down bone loss and helping your body keep bones strong.
how_to_take: Take risedronate exactly as your doctor tells you. For immediate-release tablets (Actonel): Take the tablet first thing in the morning on an empty stomach, at least 30 minutes before eating, drinking anything other than plain water, or taking any other medicines. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass (6 to 8 ounces) of plain water — do not use mineral water, coffee, tea, juice, or milk. After taking the tablet, stay sitting upright or standing for at least 30 minutes. Do not lie down. For delayed-release tablets (Atelvia): Take right after breakfast with at least 4 ounces of plain water. Stay upright for at least 30 minutes after taking it.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition. Common doses include: once daily (5 mg), once weekly (35 mg), once monthly (150 mg), or twice monthly (75 mg). Always follow your doctor's instructions and never take more than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you take risedronate once a week and miss a dose, take it the morning after you remember — but only if it is not within 2 days of your next scheduled dose. Never take two doses on the same day. If you take it once a month and miss a dose, take it the morning after you remember if your next scheduled dose is more than 7 days away. Skip the missed dose if your next dose is within 7 days. When in doubt, call your pharmacist or doctor for guidance.
storage: Store risedronate at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Do not eat, drink anything other than plain water, or take other medicines within 30 minutes of taking your risedronate dose (immediate-release). Avoid lying down for at least 30 minutes after taking the tablet, as this can cause irritation or injury to your esophagus (swallowing tube). Avoid taking calcium supplements, antacids, or vitamins at the same time as risedronate — take these at a different time of day. Avoid smoking and excess alcohol, as these can weaken your bones further.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: chest pain, heartburn, or pain when swallowing; new or unusual hip, groin, or thigh pain; jaw pain, swelling, or numbness; severe bone, joint, or muscle pain; skin rash or allergic reaction such as hives or swelling of the face or throat. Also contact your doctor if you experience eye pain or redness, or any unusual symptoms while taking this medicine.
when_it_works: Risedronate starts working in your body right away to slow bone loss, but you may not feel any different. Bone is built slowly over time, so it may take several months to years to see the full benefit. Your doctor will monitor your bone density with special tests (DEXA scans) to check how well the medicine is working. It is important to keep taking it even if you feel fine.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Risedronate is not recommended during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Kidney problems: If you have significant kidney disease, risedronate may not be safe for you. Your doctor will check your kidney function before prescribing this medicine. Older adults: Older adults can take this medicine, but should be extra careful about staying upright after each dose to reduce the risk of esophageal irritation. Children: Risedronate is generally not approved for use in children except in specific cases such as Paget's disease, and only under close medical supervision.
